streams.label: Recycling
streams.description: Clean paper, cardboard, plastic bottles and containers (#1-#5), metal cans, glass bottles and jars. Items must be empty and rinsed.

streams.label: Compost
streams.description: Food scraps, fruit and vegetable peels, coffee grounds, tea bags, soiled paper napkins, paper towels, yard waste, compostable containers marked BPI-certified.

streams.label: Landfill
streams.description: Chip bags, candy wrappers, styrofoam, plastic wrap, plastic bags, lined coffee cups, straws, mixed-material packaging, broken ceramics, diapers.

streams.label: Special Disposal
streams.description: Batteries, electronics, light bulbs, medications, paint, motor oil, hazardous chemicals. Do not place in regular bins.

streams.label: Needs Verification
streams.description: Items that cannot be confidently classified. Please ask facilities staff or check the posted signage near the bins.

overrides.note: Most paper coffee cups have a plastic lining and cannot be recycled. Remove the lid and sleeve first.
Lined paper cups are not recyclable in most facilities.
Grease-soiled cardboard should go to compost, not recycling.
Plastic bags jam sorting machinery. Some grocery stores accept them for separate recycling.
Expanded polystyrene is not accepted in most curbside recycling programs.
Batteries require special disposal. Look for a battery collection bin or take to a hazardous waste facility.
Fluorescent and CFL bulbs contain mercury. LED and incandescent bulbs can go in landfill if no special collection is available.
Used paper napkins and tissues are compostable.
Rinse before recycling. Crushing is optional.
Rinse before recycling. Remove caps if they are a different material.
Cling wrap and plastic film are not recyclable in most curbside programs.
Most takeout containers are mixed materials or food-soiled. Check if the container is marked compostable.
Flatten cardboard boxes. Remove tape and labels if possible.
All fruit and vegetable scraps are compostable.
All fruit and vegetable scraps are compostable.
Chip bags are made of mixed materials (plastic and metal foil) and are not recyclable.
Plastic straws are too small and light for recycling machinery.
Plastic utensils are not recyclable. If marked compostable (BPI-certified), they go in compost.
